facts.label: Identity and perimeter
facts.text: - Issuer and reporting entity: CCO Holdings, LLC (Delaware) with co-issuer CCO Holdings Capital Corp. (all shares held by CCO Holdings, page:1 of the June 2026 10-Q). The consolidated statements are of CCO Holdings, LLC and subsidiaries. - Ownership: 10-Q June 2026, page:1: "All of the limited liability company membership interests of CCO Holdings, LLC are held by CCH I Holdings, LLC (an indirect subsidiary of Charter Communications, Inc.". Parent, borrower and guarantor fields in the context are blank, which is not evidence of their absence. - Debt issuers and guarantors (10-Q June 2026, page:33): "Each of CCO Holdings, Charter Operating, Time Warner Cable, LLC and Time Warner Cable Enterprises LLC (collectively, the “Issuers”)" with "substantially all of Charter Operating’s direct and indirect subsidiaries" as Obligor Subsidiaries guaranteeing the debt "(other than the CCO Holdings unsecured notes)". CCO Holdings guarantees the Charter Operating notes and credit facilities (10-K page:156-158). facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The issuer's own statements support a debt-only view of leverage at 4.22x total debt and 4.20x net debt to last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of 22,251 at June 30, 2026, edging up from 4.17x and 4.16x at December 31, 2024. Cash interest cover is 4.43x on 5,024 of cash interest paid. These ratios use principal debt and company Adjusted EBITDA before the management fees that the covenants add back, so they are not covenant ratios; the filings print covenant figures only at December 31, 2025 (indenture leverage 4.0 against a 6.0 maximum, and 2.8 against 5.0 and 4.0 at Charter Operating). Operating performance is slipping slowly: Q2 2026 revenue was 13,526 against 13,766 and Adjusted EBITDA 5,428 against 5,668, with the video allocation and Cox transition costs of 65 in the quarter among the drivers the 10-Q gives. Capital spending of 5,713 in 6M 2026 against 5,273 pushed free cash flow down to 2,492 from 3,249, and distributions to parent of 2,460 took almost all of it. Three financing claims sit outside the debt figure and add to leverage if counted: the equipment installment plan facility (1,596), short-term borrowings under the deferred payment program (1,155) and operating leases (1,276 at December 31, 2025); counting the first two lifts leverage to 4.34x. The liability structure matters more than the headline ratio: 67,111 of secured debt, guaranteed by the issuer, ranks ahead of 26,734 of issuer-level unsecured notes, and the pending Cox Transactions are expected to add Cox notes to the guaranteed and secured group. Nothing after July 24, 2026 is supplied.

facts.label: Interpretation: data to risk to credit implication
facts.text: - Earnings: Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA fell 240 to 5,428, equal to the 240 fall in revenue, because operating costs excluding stock compensation were unchanged at 8,098 in both quarters (calculated: 8,236 - 138 and 8,255 - 157). Costs held flat even with 65 of Cox transition expense, so underlying costs fell. Credit implication: the EBITDA decline is a revenue problem (Internet customers down 172,000 in the quarter, Internet revenue down 3.2%, video down 9.7%) that mobile growth of 18.9% does not yet offset; leverage rises mechanically as LTM EBITDA falls. - Cash flow quality: free cash flow of 2,492 in 6M 2026 against 3,249 fell by 757, with Adjusted EBITDA down 360 and capital expenditure up 440 (10-Q Jun 2026 page:32). Capital expenditure is 21.06% of revenue in 6M 2026 against 19.17% (calculated). Credit implication: higher spending on network evolution and customer premise equipment, with rural construction at 391 in Q2 2026, is consuming the cash that would otherwise reduce debt. - Cash leakage: distributions to parent were 2,460 in 6M 2026, 6,794 in FY2025 and 5,898 over the LTM, above free cash flow of 5,827 and 5,070 in FY2025 and the LTM. The indenture test gates distributions that fund parent note principal, with leverage at 4.0 against 6.0. Credit implication: creditors rely on the parent's leverage target, not on a hard cap; any change in parent buyback policy changes the issuer's net debt directly. - Structure: of 93,845 principal debt, 54,658 of secured notes and 12,453 of credit facilities (67,111, 71.5% of the total, calculated) are guaranteed by the issuer and secured on the operating group, while 26,734 of unsecured notes sit at the issuer with no subsidiary guarantee. Credit implication: issuer unsecured holders are structurally and effectively subordinated; at 3.02x secured leverage the first call on operating cash is the secured group, and Cox notes are expected to join it. - Liquidity: availability fell to 3,700 from 4,600 in the quarter while credit facility debt rose 788 (calculated: 12,453 - 11,665), in a quarter when distributions of 1,363 exceeded free cash flow of 1,073 and notes were repurchased (the filings do not tie the borrowing to a use); the nearest facility expiry is the Revolving Loan B of about 960 on August 31, 2027, and the equipment installment plan facility's revolving period is subject to renewal (inference: about twelve months from the November 2025 amendment, so around the as-of date). Credit implication: liquidity is adequate against 1,305 of adjusted 2027 maturities but is revolver-dependent; the 2030 year-end figure of 13,868 includes 2,100 drawn on the Revolving Loan C at December 31, 2025. - Refinancing: early 2026 refinancing replaced 3,000 of 2026 and 2027 maturities with 7.000% and 7.375% notes due 2033 and 2036, coupons above the 5.500% and 5.125% retired. Cash paid for interest rose to 2,493 from 2,426 in 6M 2026, and the 10-Q attributes the rise in net interest expense (2,515 against 2,485) to higher weighted average debt. Credit implication: the run-rate coupon on refinanced maturities is higher, which would pressure cover as the 2029 and 2030 maturities are refinanced. - Evidence quality: FY2025 statements are audited (KPMG LLP, report dated January 29, 2026, 10-K page:140); quarterly statements are unaudited; Adjusted EBITDA, free cash flow and availability are management presentations; the covenant ratios are printed only at December 31, 2025.

facts.label: Sources
facts.text: Consistency with CP-0 and CP-1: this answer confirms both and refines two points. First, CP-0 and CP-1 logged the Cox cash figures of 4.0 billion (10-K) and 4.2 billion (10-Qs) without a source for the difference, and CP-0 said the components in the 10-Q do not equal 4.0 billion. The sources do explain it: the cash component payable by Charter Holdings is 500 in the Q3 2025 10-Q and the 10-K and 650 in the Q1 and Q2 2026 10-Qs, so 3,500 + 500 = 4,000 and 3,500 + 650 = 4,150, which the 2026 10-Qs round to 4.2 billion. The filings do not say why it changed. Second, the 12.6 billion assumed Cox net debt in the 10-K is stated "on a pro forma basis contemplating Cox Communications refinancing of debt maturities occurring between signing and closing", while the Q3 2025 and 2026 10-Qs give 12.4 billion without that qualifier; CP-1 reported both without this explanation. The 10-K also states that Charter, not the issuer, "is obligated to fund $4.0 billion of cash consideration" (10-K page:64), which narrows the payer question CP-1 left open (the new indebtedness issuer is still not stated). No figure in CP-0 or CP-1 is changed.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: CCO Holdings is a holding company whose principal assets are the equity of its operating subsidiaries, which deliver Spectrum Internet, Mobile, TV and Voice to residential and business customers in 41 states under a single reportable segment. It is wholly owned by CCH I Holdings, LLC and sits inside Charter's chain; it has no sponsor, no listed equity and no public ownership of its own. Its business is a mature, subscription-based, capital-intensive network operator: about 89% of revenue is monthly subscription fees, residential revenue is 77.74% of FY2025 revenue, and revenue is drifting down slightly (Q2 2026 revenue 13,526 against 13,766) because Internet and video customers are eroding faster than mobile lines and commercial revenue grow. The creditor-relevant structure is the more important feature. Of the issuer's 93,845 of principal debt at June 30, 2026, 67,111 is secured and guaranteed by the issuer and the operating group, while its own 26,734 of unsecured notes are structurally and effectively subordinated, and the issuer's subsidiaries are the primary funding source for Charter's buybacks through distributions. The transaction that matters is the pending Cox acquisition by Charter and Charter Holdings: the issuer's filings say Cox's unsecured notes are expected to become guaranteed and secured debt and Cox entities to become Obligors, which would add claims ahead of the issuer's unsecured notes while the filings do not show where Cox's earnings will sit. The Liberty Broadband Combination is a second pending parent-level transaction. Nothing is supplied after July 24, 2026, so closing status, Cox financing and any new issuance since June are unknown.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The principal transaction is the pending Cox acquisition by Charter and Charter Holdings, not by the issuer. On May 16, 2025, Charter, Charter Holdings and Cox Enterprises, Inc. entered into a Transaction Agreement under which Charter buys 100% of certain Cox Communications subsidiaries that conduct its commercial fiber and managed IT and cloud services businesses, and Cox Enterprises contributes Cox Communications' residential cable business to Charter Holdings, with Cox Enterprises paying $1.00 for a new class of Charter Class C common stock (10-Q Jun 2026 page:8). Consideration is 3.5 billion in cash from Charter for the equity sale and, for the contribution, cash from Charter Holdings plus convertible preferred units of Charter Holdings with a 6.0 billion liquidation preference paying 6.875% and about 33.6 million Charter Holdings common units; the cash from Charter Holdings is 650 million in the 2026 10-Qs and 500 million in the 10-K and the Q3 2025 10-Q (10-Q Jun 2026 page:9; 10-K page:28; 10-Q Sep 2025 page:9). The combined entity will assume Cox Communications' approximately 12.4 billion of net debt and finance leases (10-Q Jun 2026 page:9), a figure the 10-K gave as approximately 12.6 billion on a pro forma basis for Cox refinancings between signing and closing (10-K page:28). The status is pending: the June 2026 10-Q uses the future tense throughout, lists the ability to satisfy closing conditions among its risks and gives no closing date; the 10-K lists conditions including Charter stockholder approvals, expiry of the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period and approvals of the Federal Communications Commission and certain local franchise, state franchising and state public utility commission authorities (10-K page:61). Which approvals have been received, the end date and the termination fee amounts are not in the pack (the 10-K says only that Charter "could owe a substantial termination fee" (10-K page:62)).

The status is pending: the June 2026 10-Q uses the future tense throughout, lists the ability to satisfy closing conditions among its risks and gives no closing date; the 10-K lists conditions including Charter stockholder approvals, expiry of the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period and approvals of the Federal Communications Commission and certain local franchise, state franchising and state public utility commission authorities (10-K page:61). Which approvals have been received, the end date and the termination fee amounts are not in the pack (the 10-K says only that Charter "could owe a substantial termination fee" (10-K page:62)).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: For creditors the key text is the issuer's own: the 10-Q says the company is "also required to fund approximately $4.2 billion of cash purchase price at the closing of the Cox Transactions" (10-Q Jun 2026 page:27), while the 10-K says "Charter is obligated to fund $4.0 billion of cash consideration under the Transaction Agreement which we expect to fund by incurring indebtedness" (10-K page:64). After closing the issuer "presently expect[s]" that Cox's unsecured notes assumed at closing "will constitute Guaranteed and Secured Debt", that Cox Communications and substantially all of its subsidiaries "will become Obligors", and that all or part of the approximately 4.2 billion of indebtedness issued to finance the cash payment "may constitute Guaranteed and Secured Debt when issued" (10-Q Jun 2026 page:34). Charter and its subsidiaries, including CCO Holdings, are also subject to restrictions on the conduct of their business before closing, including in certain cases the ability to incur certain indebtedness (10-K page:65). The contribution is to Charter Holdings (10-Q Jun 2026 page:8), and the filings do not say whether Cox's operating results will be consolidated in CCO Holdings' statements after closing or sit elsewhere in Charter's structure. That is Insufficient Information, not an adverse conclusion; it matters because Cox debt could be guaranteed inside the Obligor Group, which the issuer guarantees, while Cox earnings might not be in the issuer's own statements. The cash-purchase financing is described only as debt to be incurred; no sources and uses, commitment papers, rating agency actions or liquidity effect are given. Cox transition costs are already in operating results (65 in Q2 2026 and 89 in 6M 2026) with 34 and 37 of transition capital expenditure (10-Q Jun 2026 page:14 to page:15, page:37).

facts.text: The second pending transaction is the Liberty Broadband Combination, a merger agreement dated November 12, 2024 under which Charter acquires Liberty Broadband Corporation through a merger and upstream merger, with Liberty Broadband becoming a wholly owned subsidiary of Charter (10-Q Jun 2026 page:28). Pending its closing, Charter buys Charter Class A shares from Liberty Broadband monthly, and in May 2026 Charter advanced a term loan of approximately 359 million to Liberty Broadband (10-Q Jun 2026 page:29 to page:30). The 10-K expects additional debt "in connection with the Cox Transactions and Liberty Broadband Combination" and the assumption of indebtedness of Liberty Broadband and its subsidiaries (10-K page:52). The amount and ranking of any Liberty Broadband debt are not stated.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: New debt issues in the periods covered: in September 2025 Charter Operating and Charter Communications Operating Capital Corp. jointly issued 1.25 billion of 5.850% senior secured notes due December 2035 at 99.932% and 750 million of 6.700% senior secured notes due December 2055 at 99.832%, with proceeds used for general corporate purposes including repayment of the 6.150% senior secured notes due 2026 and potential buybacks, and a loss on extinguishment of about 28 million (10-K page:155). In January 2026 CCO Holdings and CCO Holdings Capital Corp. jointly issued 1.75 billion of 7.000% senior notes due February 2033 and 1.25 billion of 7.375% senior notes due February 2036, both at par, with proceeds for general corporate purposes including the call of 750 million of the 5.500% notes due 2026 and part (2.25 billion) of the 5.125% notes due 2027 (10-K page:155; 10-Q Mar 2026 page:11). In November 2025 the equipment installment plan facility was amended to extend maturity to November 3, 2029 and raise capacity to 2.0 billion (10-K page:161). In the second quarter of 2026 the company repurchased 1.2 billion of principal of various series on the open market at a gain of about 243 million (10-Q Jun 2026 page:11). No new notes are reported for the first half of 2026 other than the January issuance, and no source reports issuance after June 30, 2026.

Internet customers fell to 29,388 thousand from 29,908 thousand while mobile lines rose to 12,540 thousand from 10,856 thousand over twelve months.
The issuer's subsidiaries are the primary funding source for Charter's share repurchases through distributions to parent companies.
The Cox Transactions are pending; the issuer's filings expect Cox notes to become guaranteed and secured debt, and the Cox cash figure moved from 4.0 billion to 4.2 billion.
In 2026 unsecured notes fell 516 while credit facilities rose 504.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: CCO HOLDINGS LLC is a large, cash-generative but leveraged cable credit whose earnings are eroding slowly and whose structure and pending acquisition decide its direction. The strongest support is USD 22,251 million of last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA at a 40.91% margin, cash interest cover of 4.43x and liquidity of USD 3,985 million, with little principal due before 2028. The weakest point is USD 93,845 million of debt at 4.22x, of which USD 26,734 million of unsecured notes sit behind USD 67,111 million of secured debt (3.02x), while distributions to the parent exceeded free cash flow. What decides the outcome is the Cox closing: how it is financed, whether Cox debt joins the guaranteed and secured group, and the parent's leverage policy afterwards. None of that is in the sources after July 24, 2026.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, leverage is steady near 4.2x and drifting up through earnings, not borrowing. CCO HOLDINGS LLC had total debt of USD 93,845 million and net debt of USD 93,560 million at June 30, 2026, which are 4.22x and 4.20x of last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 22,251 million, against 4.17x and 4.16x at December 31, 2024 [CP-1]. Debt fell USD 772 million in the half while last-twelve-months EBITDA fell from USD 22,611 million at FY2025, so the ratio rose from 4.18x. At constant debt, an EBITDA decline of 5%, 10% or 15% would take the ratio to 4.44x, 4.69x or 4.96x (calculated, illustrative). These are principal-debt ratios on company Adjusted EBITDA before the management fees that the covenants add back; they are not the covenant ratios, which the 10-K printed only at December 31, 2025: 4.0x against a 6.0x indenture maximum and 2.8x against 5.0x and 4.0x at Charter Operating [CP-1; Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation].

Q2 2026 revenue was USD 13,526 million against USD 13,766 million and Adjusted EBITDA USD 5,428 million against USD 5,668 million, a fall of 4.2%; operating costs excluding stock compensation were flat at USD 8,098 million despite USD 65 million of Cox transition expenses [CP-1]. Internet customers fell by 172,000 in the quarter while mobile lines rose by 406,000, Internet revenue fell 3.2% and video revenue 9.7%, and mobile service revenue rose 18.9% [CP-1A]. The business faces fibre overlap from AT&T and Verizon in about 27% and 16% of the footprint and fixed wireless competition [CP-1A]. The mechanism is that a low-lock-in subscription base loses revenue faster than a largely fixed network cost base can adjust, so leverage rises as EBITDA falls (Analyst Interpretation).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Third, cash flow after capital spending is thin and is distributed to the parent. Last-twelve-months free cash flow was USD 5,070 million, or 5.40% of principal debt, after capital expenditure of USD 12,064 million, which is 54.22% of EBITDA [CP-1; calculated]. EBITDA less capital expenditure of USD 10,187 million covers cash interest of USD 5,024 million 2.03x (calculated). Distributions to the parent were USD 5,898 million over the last twelve months and USD 6,794 million in FY2025, against free cash flow of USD 5,070 million and USD 5,827 million, a shortfall of USD 828 million and USD 967 million (calculated); principal debt rose USD 838 million in FY2025 [CP-1]. In the first half of 2026 distributions of USD 2,460 million were close to free cash flow of USD 2,492 million. The 10-Q says the issuer and its subsidiaries are "the primary source" of funding for Charter's buybacks through distributions [CP-1A]. This is a policy choice, limited by an indenture leverage test (4.0x against 6.0x at December 31, 2025) and by Charter's stated 4.0x to 4.5x net leverage range, not by a hard cap (Analyst Interpretation).

facts.text: Fourth, the unsecured notes are structurally and effectively subordinated, and the layers are thin in turns of EBITDA. Of USD 93,845 million of principal debt, USD 67,111 million (71.5%) is senior secured notes, debentures and credit facilities guaranteed by CCO Holdings and the operating group, and USD 26,734 million is CCO Holdings senior unsecured notes with no subsidiary guarantee [CP-1; CP-1A]. Secured debt is 3.02x of EBITDA and total debt 4.22x, so the unsecured notes occupy the part of the capital structure between 3.02x and 4.22x (calculated). Between December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026, unsecured notes fell USD 516 million while credit facilities rose USD 504 million, so debt shifted from unsecured to secured [CP-1; CP-1A]. This is a mechanic, not a recovery view: collateral coverage is not computed and executed documents are not supplied.

facts.text: Fifth, liquidity is adequate and near-term maturities are modest, but refinancing concentrates in 2029 and 2030. Cash of USD 285 million and availability of about USD 3,700 million give liquidity of USD 3,985 million, which is 3.99x the USD 999 million current portion of debt (calculated) [CP-1]. Scheduled principal was USD 1,055 million for 2026 and USD 3,555 million for 2027 at December 31, 2025; after the February 2026 redemptions of USD 750 million and USD 2,250 million these become USD 305 million and USD 1,305 million before 2026 amortisation already paid and the unallocated repurchases, with 2028 at USD 5,392 million, 2029 at USD 7,279 million and 2030 at USD 13,868 million [CP-1]. The 2029 and 2030 amounts together are USD 21,147 million, 22.35% of year-end principal debt (calculated). The Revolving Loan B of about USD 960 million matures on August 31, 2027, within twelve months of the as-of date, and the equipment installment plan facility's revolving period is subject to renewal around the as-of date (inference from the November 2025 amendment) [CP-1].

facts.text: Sixth, refinancing and floating-rate exposure raise cost over time. The 87% of debt that was fixed at December 31, 2025 had an average rate of 5.07%, and the 13% that floats had a forward-implied average of 5.36%; Item 7A describes only cross-currency swaps on the sterling notes and no interest rate derivatives (10-K page:105). A 1.00% move on the USD 12,453 million of credit facility debt would change annual interest by about USD 125 million, 2.5% of last-twelve-months cash interest of USD 5,024 million (calculated, before floors). The January 2026 notes carry 7.000% and 7.375% coupons against 5.500% and 5.125% on the USD 3,000 million redeemed, an annual coupon increase of about USD 58 million before the interest saved on the USD 1,249 million of repurchases, whose coupons are not disclosed (calculated). The 10-K scheduled USD 4,817 million of interest for 2026 and USD 4,646 million for 2027 on the year-end debt before those events (10-K page:160).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Seventh, the Cox Transactions and the Liberty Broadband Combination are the largest open items. The issuer's 10-Q expects Cox's unsecured notes to become guaranteed and secured debt, Cox entities to become Obligors and all or part of about USD 4.2 billion of new debt to do the same; the cash consideration is USD 4.0 billion in the 10-K and about USD 4.2 billion in the 2026 10-Qs, which tracks Charter Holdings' cash payment moving from USD 500 million to USD 650 million, and the assumed Cox net debt and finance leases are USD 12.4 billion in the 10-Qs and USD 12.6 billion on a pro forma basis in the 10-K [CP-1A]. The filings do not say where Cox earnings will sit relative to the issuer, who issues the new debt, or whether any approval has been received. That is a missing datapoint, not an adverse finding; it decides whether the issuer's secured layer grows while its own EBITDA base does not (Insufficient Information and Analyst Interpretation).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. (1) Scale and stable margin: USD 22,251 million of last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA at a 40.91% margin across 41 states, with revenue of USD 54,396 million (Documentary Fact; CP-1, CP-1A). (2) Debt service capacity: cash interest cover of 4.43x and EBITDA less capital expenditure covering cash interest 2.03x (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (3) Liquidity and a long-dated profile: USD 3,985 million of liquidity, USD 305 million and USD 1,305 million of scheduled principal for 2026 and 2027 after the February 2026 redemptions, and 67.08% of year-end principal debt due after 2030 (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (4) Mostly fixed-rate debt: 87% of principal at year-end, which limits rate sensitivity to about USD 125 million per 1.00% on the floating part (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (5) Visible covenant room at the last printed date: 4.0x against 6.0x and 2.8x against 5.0x and 4.0x at December 31, 2025 (Documentary Fact; CP-1). (6) Growth segments: mobile lines up 1,684 thousand over twelve months and mobile service revenue up 18.9% in Q2 2026 (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (7) Clean audited disclosure: an unqualified KPMG LLP opinion on FY2025 and regular debt, guarantor and reconciliation disclosure (Documentary Fact; CP-1A).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. (1) Leverage above 4x and rising slowly: 4.22x on debt and 4.34x including the equipment installment plan facility and short-term borrowings, with Adjusted EBITDA down 4.2% in Q2 2026 (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (2) Cash leakage above free cash flow: USD 5,898 million of distributions against USD 5,070 million over the last twelve months, and free cash flow down to USD 2,492 million from USD 3,249 million in the half (Documentary Fact; CP-1). (3) Subordinated unsecured notes: USD 26,734 million behind USD 67,111 million of secured debt, with debt shifting toward secured credit facilities in 2026 (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1, CP-1A). (4) Refinancing concentration and cost: USD 21,147 million due in 2029 and 2030 and about USD 58 million more annual coupon on the early 2026 refinancing (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (5) Capital intensity and intangible-heavy assets: capital expenditure of USD 12,064 million is 54.22% of EBITDA, and franchises and goodwill are 63.34% of total assets, with a fair-value cushion of more than 10% at the last impairment test (Documentary Fact; CP-1, CP-1A). (6) Competition and customer losses: Internet and video customers falling against fibre and fixed wireless entrants (Documentary Fact and Management Language; CP-1A). (7) Opaque post-closing structure and missing documents: Cox financing, perimeter and approvals not supplied; indentures, credit agreement and covenant definitions not supplied (Insufficient Information; CP-0, CP-1A). (8) Claims outside debt of USD 1,596 million of equipment installment plan financing and USD 1,155 million of short-term borrowings, USD 725 million of supply chain finance and USD 1,276 million of operating leases that are not in the debt figure (Documentary Fact; CP-1).

- Coupon change on the early 2026 refinancing: new 1,750 x 7.000% + 1,250 x 7.375% = 122.5 + 92.2 = 214.7; retired 750 x 5.500% + 2,250 x 5.125% = 41.3 + 115.3 = 156.6; difference 58.1 per year (gross, before the saving on the 1,249 of repurchases, series and coupons unknown).

- Covenant headroom from printed December 31, 2025 ratios: indenture 6.0 - 4.0 = 2.0 turns, 1 - 4.0 / 6.0 = 33%; credit facility total 5.0 - 2.8 = 2.2 turns, 1 - 2.8 / 5.0 = 44%; first lien 4.0 - 2.8 = 1.2 turns, 1 - 2.8 / 4.0 = 30% (constant debt; ratios rounded).
- Capital structure layers (June 30, 2026): secured 54,658 + 12,453 = 67,111, 71.5% of 93,845; unsecured 26,734, 28.5%.

rows.label: CCO Holdings is a large, cash-generative but leveraged cable credit: debt is 4.22x EBITDA and cash interest cover is 4.43x, with USD 3,985 million of liquidity. Its unsecured notes sit behind secured debt, and the Cox closing is unresolved.
Debt of USD 93,845 million is 4.22x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 22,251 million, slightly above 4.17x at December 31, 2024, as EBITDA slips.
Distributions to parent of USD 5,898 million exceeded free cash flow of USD 5,070 million over the last twelve months.
USD 26,734 million of unsecured notes rank behind USD 67,111 million of secured debt, which is 3.02x EBITDA, while total debt is 4.22x.
Debt maturing is USD 7,279 million in 2029 and USD 13,868 million in 2030, and early 2026 refinancing added about USD 58 million of annual coupon.
The Cox Transactions are pending and the post-closing perimeter and financing are not described beyond expectations in the 10-Q.

Fundamental view: stable operating cash generation and adequate liquidity with a long-dated debt profile, offset by leverage above 4x, slowly falling EBITDA, parent cash leakage above free cash flow, structurally and effectively subordinated unsecured notes and an unresolved acquisition. Not a rating and not a recommendation.

Cash also differs: "$509 million cash position" for Charter (release page:7) versus "$285 million" for the issuer (10-Q June 2026, page:36). The 10-Q controls for issuer facts.

- Use: the releases add quarter narrative, customer data, parent leverage and a statement that "$1.2 billion in aggregate principal amount of Charter Communications Operating, LLC and CCO Holdings, LLC notes" were repurchased for "$1.0 billion in cash" (release page:1). The January release also records the January 2026 issuance by CCO Holdings of $1.75 billion 7.000% senior notes due February 2033 and $1.25 billion 7.375% senior notes due February 2036 (release page:7), which the 10-K also states (page:104 and page:155).
### Information-availability boundary
- All sources predate the as-of date and cutoff. The latest is the June 2026 10-Q and release, dated July 24, 2026.

- Nothing dated after July 24, 2026 is supplied. The pack retrieval record lists the June 2026 10-Q as the latest of the three newest 10-Qs, so no 10-Q for the September 2026 quarter is in the pack. Whether one was filed before 2026-11-05 cannot be determined from the supplied text. Events in the window July 25 to November 5, 2026, including Cox closing status, are Not supplied, not absent.
- The Q3 2025 10-Q is a comparative, not a current-period source.
### Identity and perimeter

- Issuer and reporting entity: CCO Holdings, LLC (Delaware) with co-issuer CCO Holdings Capital Corp. (all shares held by CCO Holdings, page:1 of the June 2026 10-Q). The consolidated statements are of CCO Holdings, LLC and subsidiaries.

- Ownership: 10-Q June 2026, page:1: "All of the limited liability company membership interests of CCO Holdings, LLC are held by CCH I Holdings, LLC (an indirect subsidiary of Charter Communications, Inc.". Parent, borrower and guarantor fields in the context are blank, which is not evidence of their absence.

- Debt issuers and guarantors (10-Q June 2026, page:33): "Each of CCO Holdings, Charter Operating, Time Warner Cable, LLC and Time Warner Cable Enterprises LLC (collectively, the “Issuers”)" with "substantially all of Charter Operating’s direct and indirect subsidiaries" as Obligor Subsidiaries guaranteeing the debt "(other than the CCO Holdings unsecured notes)". CCO Holdings guarantees the Charter Operating notes and credit facilities (10-K page:156-158). The Charter Operating credit facilities are the secured layer; the CCO Holdings notes are senior unsecured and "structurally subordinated to all obligations of subsidiaries" (10-K page:155).

- Outside the guarantor group: CCO EIP Financing, LLC, a bankruptcy-remote consolidated vehicle with a senior secured equipment installment plan facility (10-Q June 2026, page:11-12 and page:35). Its carrying value is a separate balance sheet line from long-term debt (page:5).

- Parent-level transactions that do not change the issuer's statements yet: the Cox Transactions (Transaction Agreement of May 16, 2025, 10-Q June 2026, page:8-9) and the Liberty Broadband Combination (page:28). The 10-Q states Cox Communications' notes are expected after closing to "constitute Guaranteed and Secured Debt" and Cox entities to "become Obligors" (page:34).
### Document conflicts and updates

| Cox debt to be assumed | 10-K page:64: "approximately $12.6 billion of Cox Communications’ outstanding net debt and finance leases" | 10-Q June 2026 page:9: "approximately $12.4 billion in outstanding net debt and finance leases" | Different dates and wording; the later filing is the more recent statement. CP-1A and CP-2 must show both and not pick one silently. |

| Cash to fund at Cox closing | 10-K page:64: "obligated to fund $4.0 billion of cash consideration" | 10-Q June 2026 page:27: "approximately $4.2 billion of cash purchase price"; page:8-9 lists $3.5 billion and $650 million | CP-2 must carry the stated amounts with their dates; the components in the 10-Q do not equal the $4.0 billion in the 10-K. |

| Year-end availability under credit facilities | 10-K page:104: "approximately $4.4 billion as of December 31, 2025" | 10-Q June 2026 page:11: "approximately $3.7 billion as of June 30, 2026" (March 31, 2026: approximately $4.6 billion, 10-Q March 2026 page:11) | Not a conflict; different dates. A letters-of-credit split is available only at year-end (10-K page:157, page:182). |
### Consumer evidence demand

| CP-1 | Annual and interim statements, debt, liquidity, cash interest, Adjusted EBITDA, free cash flow | 10-K page:140-141, 91, 102-104, 154-160; 10-Q June 2026 page:5-7, 10-11, 26; 10-Q March 2026 page:5-6, 18, 24; 10-Q Sept 2025 page:5-6 | Series list and maturity ladder only as of December 31, 2025; no discrete third and fourth quarter 2025 statements (nine-month and full-year only); text conversion |

| CP-1A | Business, segments, ownership, guarantor structure, transactions | 10-K page:5, 98-100; 10-Q June 2026 page:7-9, 16-19, 33-35 | Cox transaction agreement, Liberty Broadband merger agreement and Exhibit 22.1 are not supplied |

| CP-5 | Traceable claims | All seven filings and releases carry page chunks | Original HTML and XBRL not supplied; releases are parent perimeter |
### Analytical read-through

- Usable coverage: the issuer's audited FY2025 statements and unaudited statements to June 30, 2026, with comparatives, support a reported financial foundation, including a last-twelve-months view to be built by CP-1 from the year and the two six-month periods. Evidence is the issuer's own 10-K (page:141) and 10-Q (page:5-6), not the parent's releases.

- Strongest contrary evidence: the pending Cox Transactions and Liberty Broadband Combination. The 10-Q states Charter will "fund approximately $4.2 billion of cash purchase price at the closing" (page:27) and expects Cox entities to become Obligors (page:34). Source risk mechanism: the supplied filings describe the post-closing guarantor group and debt only as expectations, so any capital structure built from them is a pre-closing view. Downstream consequence: CP-1A and CP-2 must label closing-dependent items as unrealized and must not treat parent leverage statements, such as Charter's "4.18 times" (10-Q June 2026 page:27), as issuer leverage.

- Perimeter mechanism: the releases and some 10-Q text are written at Charter level (net income attributable to Charter shareholders, Charter's leverage ratio, share repurchases), while the debt, interest and cash sit in the issuer. A consumer that mixes the two overstates or understates earnings and cash.

- Debt-detail mechanism: the series table is at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:102-103). The 10-Qs report only three classes and describe February 2026 redemptions of $750 million and $2.25 billion and $1.2 billion of repurchases of "various series" without series names (10-Q June 2026 page:11). CP-1 cannot rebuild an exact current maturity ladder without a disclosed series list; it can show the year-end ladder and the stated post-year-end events.

- Other claims outside debt, located for CP-2: operating leases and their maturities (10-K page:154), supply chain finance and deferred payment programs (10-Q June 2026 page:9-10), the equipment installment plan facility (page:11-12), letters of credit and surety bonds (10-K page:182), and cross-currency derivatives (10-Q June 2026 page:13). Pension plan settlement detail appears in the 10-K (page:184-185) and is not repeated in the 10-Qs.
- What cannot proceed: covenant headroom measured on executed definitions, current series-level maturity ladder, Cox closing structure, any view after July 24, 2026.

- Next evidence action: supply the Charter Operating credit agreement and the CCO Holdings and Charter Operating indentures, Exhibit 22.1 of the June 2026 10-Q, the Cox Transaction Agreement and any financing commitments, any 10-Q and 8-Ks filed from July 25, 2026 to the cutoff, and the issuer's Q3 2026 release if it exists.
## Calculations

No new calculation. CP-0 does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. Every figure above is quoted from a located page. Differences such as $4.0 billion versus $4.2 billion are reported as stated, not derived.
## Gaps

| No filing or release after July 24, 2026 (the September 2026 quarter and events to the cutoff, including Cox closing status) | High | CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply the third quarter 2026 10-Q and any 8-K from July 25 to November 5, 2026, or confirm none exists |

| Executed indentures, Charter Operating credit agreement and covenant definitions not supplied (context legal_documents is "none") | High for legal work; Medium for CP-2 | CP-2 | Supply the executed documents or the 10-K exhibit versions |

| Series-level debt list and maturity ladder only as of December 31, 2025; February 2026 redemptions identified by series but $1.2 billion repurchases are "various series" | High | CP-1, CP-2 | Supply a current debt schedule or a later 10-K/10-Q debt note with series detail |

| Letters of credit and revolver split only at year-end (10-K page:157, page:182); the June 2026 10-Q gives only total availability | Medium | CP-1, CP-2 | Supply facility-level availability and letters of credit at the latest date |

| Covenant ratios for Charter Operating and indenture leverage stated only at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:156, page:158); later 10-Qs say the test was met without figures | Medium | CP-2 | Supply compliance certificates or later covenant disclosure |
| Cox Transaction Agreement, Liberty Broadband merger agreement and Exhibit 22.1 not supplied | Medium | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply the agreements and the exhibit |
| Earnings releases are Charter-level; no issuer-level release exists in the pack | Medium | CP-1, CP-5 | Use the issuer 10-Q for issuer facts and label release data as parent |
| No discrete fourth quarter 2025 statements; only full-year (10-K) and nine-month (Q3 2025 10-Q) | Low | CP-1 | Build the fourth quarter only by labelled difference, as CP-1 decides |
| No rating agency reports; the filings say only "Our split credit rating" (10-Q June 2026 page:26) | Low for selected modules | CP-2 | Not required for this scope; keep Not supplied |
| Text conversion only; original HTML and XBRL not supplied, and extraction is not a fidelity review | Low | CP-1, CP-5 | Check flagged tables against the filed HTML when available |
## Next module

- CP-1: treat the issuer's 10-K and 10-Qs as controlling; show FY2025, six months and three months to June 30, 2026 as separate labelled periods; keep the parent's releases as labelled context only; carry the year-end series table with the February 2026 redemptions and $1.2 billion repurchases as stated events; keep the equipment installment plan facility, supply chain finance and deferred payment program separate from debt and say whether each is inside the debt figure.

- CP-1A: carry the ownership chain, guarantor and collateral structure and the pending Cox Transactions and Liberty Broadband Combination as unclosed; show both the $12.6 billion and $12.4 billion Cox debt statements and the $4.0 billion and $4.2 billion cash figures with their dates.

- CP-2 and CP-5: carry the missing executed documents, the lack of post-July 24, 2026 evidence and the perimeter mismatch of the releases as restrictions; do not present closing-dependent structure as current.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Debt is 4.22x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA at June 30, 2026 (4.17x at December 31, 2024), with cash interest cover of 4.43x. Free cash flow and revolver availability fell in 2026; distributions to parent exceeded free cash flow. | Medium | Adjusted EBITDA is a company non-GAAP measure; current series-level debt, covenant ratios and events after July 24, 2026 are not in the sources. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Free cash flow was 2,492 in 6M 2026 against 3,249 in 6M 2025, because Adjusted EBITDA fell and capital spending rose. | Less internal cash to fund debt reduction; leverage depends on EBITDA holding up. | High |

| Distributions to parent were 2,460 in 6M 2026, close to free cash flow of 2,492, and 5,898 over the last twelve months against free cash flow of 5,070. | Cash is upstreamed to the parent, so debt paydown depends on parent choices, limited only by indenture tests. | Medium |

| Revolver availability was 3,700 at June 30, 2026 against 4,600 at March 31, 2026, while credit facility debt rose to 12,453 from 11,665. | The liquidity cushion is thinner, and a revolver tranche of about 960 matures August 31, 2027. | Medium |

| Secured debt of 67,111 ranks ahead of 26,734 of unsecured notes at the issuer, which are structurally subordinated; secured debt is 3.02x EBITDA. | Unsecured holders sit behind roughly three turns of secured leverage; expected Cox debt may join the secured group. | High |

| Debt maturing is 7,279 in 2029 and 13,868 in 2030 on the year-end schedule, after only 1,055 in 2026 and 3,555 in 2027. | Refinancing risk concentrates in 2029 and 2030; all 750 of the 2026 notes and 2,250 of the 2027 notes were redeemed in February 2026. | Medium |
### Financial base view

The issuer's own statements support a debt-only view of leverage at 4.22x total debt and 4.20x net debt to last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of 22,251 at June 30, 2026, edging up from 4.17x and 4.16x at December 31, 2024. Cash interest cover is 4.43x on 5,024 of cash interest paid. These ratios use principal debt and company Adjusted EBITDA before the management fees that the covenants add back, so they are not covenant ratios; the filings print covenant figures only at December 31, 2025 (indenture leverage 4.0 against a 6.0 maximum, and 2.8 against 5.0 and 4.0 at Charter Operating). Operating performance is slipping slowly: Q2 2026 revenue was 13,526 against 13,766 and Adjusted EBITDA 5,428 against 5,668, with the video allocation and Cox transition costs of 65 in the quarter among the drivers the 10-Q gives. Capital spending of 5,713 in 6M 2026 against 5,273 pushed free cash flow down to 2,492 from 3,249, and distributions to parent of 2,460 took almost all of it. Three financing claims sit outside the debt figure and add to leverage if counted: the equipment installment plan facility (1,596), short-term borrowings under the deferred payment program (1,155) and operating leases (1,276 at December 31, 2025); counting the first two lifts leverage to 4.34x. The liability structure matters more than the headline ratio: 67,111 of secured debt, guaranteed by the issuer, ranks ahead of 26,734 of issuer-level unsecured notes, and the pending Cox Transactions are expected to add Cox notes to the guaranteed and secured group. Nothing after July 24, 2026 is supplied.

The equipment installment plan facility was amended in November 2025 to extend maturity and raise capacity to 2.0 billion (10-K page:161).

- Cox Transactions (parent-level, pending): Transaction Agreement of May 16, 2025; Charter pays 3.5 billion and Charter Holdings pays 650 million in cash plus 6.0 billion of convertible preferred units at 6.875%; the combined entity assumes about 12.4 billion of Cox net debt and finance leases (10-Q Jun 2026 page:8-9). The issuer's 10-Q states it is "required to fund approximately $4.2 billion of cash purchase price at the closing" (page:27) and that after closing Cox notes are expected to become guaranteed and secured debt with Cox entities becoming Obligors, and that all or part of the 4.2 billion of new indebtedness may do the same (page:34). The 10-K figures were 12.6 billion of assumed net debt and 4.0 billion of cash consideration (10-K page:64). Transition expenses were 65 in Q2 2026 and 89 in 6M 2026 in operating costs, plus 34 and 37 of transition capital expenditure (10-Q Jun 2026 page:14-15, page:37). Closing status after July 24, 2026 is not supplied.

- Liberty Broadband Combination (parent-level, pending): Merger Agreement of November 12, 2024; in May 2026 Charter advanced a term loan of about 359 to Liberty Broadband (10-Q Jun 2026 page:28, page:30).

- Management guidance changed direction: the 10-K said "we expect to increase the total amount of our indebtedness to maintain leverage within Charter's target leverage range" with a post-closing long-term target of 3.5 to 3.75 times (10-K page:93); the June 2026 10-Q says "We currently expect to decrease the total amount of our indebtedness to achieve Charter's target leverage" with a post-closing target of 3.5 times (10-Q Jun 2026 page:27). Full-year 2026 capital expenditure is expected at about 11.4 billion excluding Cox (10-Q Jun 2026 page:37).

- Comparability: the "seamless entertainment allocation" reduced Q2 2026 video revenue by 184 and 6M video revenue by 355 and lowers programming costs by the same amounts (10-Q Jun 2026 page:22, page:24), so on the 10-Q's description it moves revenue and costs equally and does not change Adjusted EBITDA (inference). Q2 2025 other revenue included a one-time 45 benefit (page:23). 6M 2025 other operating expenses included a 105 loss on disposal of assets (page:15).
- Events after June 30, 2026 up to the cutoff: none stated in the pinned sources; nothing after July 24, 2026 is supplied.
### Interpretation: data to risk to credit implication

- Earnings: Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA fell 240 to 5,428, equal to the 240 fall in revenue, because operating costs excluding stock compensation were unchanged at 8,098 in both quarters (calculated: 8,236 - 138 and 8,255 - 157). Costs held flat even with 65 of Cox transition expense, so underlying costs fell. Credit implication: the EBITDA decline is a revenue problem (Internet customers down 172,000 in the quarter, Internet revenue down 3.2%, video down 9.7%) that mobile growth of 18.9% does not yet offset; leverage rises mechanically as LTM EBITDA falls.

- Cash flow quality: free cash flow of 2,492 in 6M 2026 against 3,249 fell by 757, with Adjusted EBITDA down 360 and capital expenditure up 440 (10-Q Jun 2026 page:32). Capital expenditure is 21.06% of revenue in 6M 2026 against 19.17% (calculated). Credit implication: higher spending on network evolution and customer premise equipment, with rural construction at 391 in Q2 2026, is consuming the cash that would otherwise reduce debt.

- Cash leakage: distributions to parent were 2,460 in 6M 2026, 6,794 in FY2025 and 5,898 over the LTM, above free cash flow of 5,827 and 5,070 in FY2025 and the LTM. The indenture test gates distributions that fund parent note principal, with leverage at 4.0 against 6.0. Credit implication: creditors rely on the parent's leverage target, not on a hard cap; any change in parent buyback policy changes the issuer's net debt directly.

- Structure: of 93,845 principal debt, 54,658 of secured notes and 12,453 of credit facilities (67,111, 71.5% of the total, calculated) are guaranteed by the issuer and secured on the operating group, while 26,734 of unsecured notes sit at the issuer with no subsidiary guarantee. Credit implication: issuer unsecured holders are structurally and effectively subordinated; at 3.02x secured leverage the first call on operating cash is the secured group, and Cox notes are expected to join it.

- Liquidity: availability fell to 3,700 from 4,600 in the quarter while credit facility debt rose 788 (calculated: 12,453 - 11,665), in a quarter when distributions of 1,363 exceeded free cash flow of 1,073 and notes were repurchased (the filings do not tie the borrowing to a use); the nearest facility expiry is the Revolving Loan B of about 960 on August 31, 2027, and the equipment installment plan facility's revolving period is subject to renewal (inference: about twelve months from the November 2025 amendment, so around the as-of date). Credit implication: liquidity is adequate against 1,305 of adjusted 2027 maturities but is revolver-dependent; the 2030 year-end figure of 13,868 includes 2,100 drawn on the Revolving Loan C at December 31, 2025.

- Refinancing: early 2026 refinancing replaced 3,000 of 2026 and 2027 maturities with 7.000% and 7.375% notes due 2033 and 2036, coupons above the 5.500% and 5.125% retired. Cash paid for interest rose to 2,493 from 2,426 in 6M 2026, and the 10-Q attributes the rise in net interest expense (2,515 against 2,485) to higher weighted average debt. Credit implication: the run-rate coupon on refinanced maturities is higher, which would pressure cover as the 2029 and 2030 maturities are refinanced.

- Evidence quality: FY2025 statements are audited (KPMG LLP, report dated January 29, 2026, 10-K page:140); quarterly statements are unaudited; Adjusted EBITDA, free cash flow and availability are management presentations; the covenant ratios are printed only at December 31, 2025.
## Calculations
All inputs are US$ millions from the cited pages. Computed with exact arithmetic and rounded to the precision shown.
### LTM Adjusted EBITDA
### LTM and discrete flow lines

- Revenues LTM: 54,774 + 27,123 - 27,501 = 54,396. Operating costs LTM: 32,836 + 16,418 - 16,474 = 32,780. D&A LTM: 8,681 + 4,393 - 4,342 = 8,732. Other operating expenses LTM: 432 + 66 - 209 = 289. Income from operations LTM: 12,825 + 6,246 - 6,476 = 12,595. Interest expense, net LTM: 5,004 + 2,515 - 2,485 = 5,034. Net income attributable LTM: 7,440 + 3,779 - 3,767 = 7,452.
- Growth check against the 10-Q: Q2 revenue 13,526 / 13,766 - 1 = -1.74% (printed (1.7)%); Q2 Adjusted EBITDA 5,428 / 5,668 - 1 = -4.23% (printed (4.2)%).
- Operating costs excluding stock compensation: Q2 2026 8,236 - 138 = 8,098; Q2 2025 8,255 - 157 = 8,098.
### Leverage, cover and ratios

- Extended leverage: (debt + equipment installment plan facility + short-term borrowings) / Adjusted EBITDA: FY2024 (93,779 + 1,072 + 758) = 95,609 / 22,476 = 4.25x; FY2025 (94,617 + 1,447 + 918) = 96,982 / 22,611 = 4.29x; LTM Q2 2026 (93,845 + 1,596 + 1,155) = 96,596 / 22,251 = 4.34x. Operating leases (1,276 at December 31, 2025) are not added.

- Covenant proxy at December 31, 2025: secured 67,367 / (22,611 + 1,400) = 2.81x; total debt 94,617 / 24,011 = 3.94x; total plus equipment installment plan facility (94,617 + 1,447) / 24,011 = 4.00x. Headroom: indenture 6.0 - 4.0 = 2.0 turns and 1 - 4.0 / 6.0 = 33%; credit facility 5.0 - 2.8 = 2.2 turns and 1 - 2.8 / 5.0 = 44%; first lien 4.0 - 2.8 = 1.2 turns and 1 - 2.8 / 4.0 = 30% (debt held constant; printed ratios are rounded).
### Liquidity

- Liquidity (cash plus printed availability): Q3 2025 235 + 4,000 = 4,235; FY2025 218 + 4,400 = 4,618; Q1 2026 246 + 4,600 = 4,846; Q2 2026 285 + 3,700 = 3,985. Availability is printed to 0.1 billion, so each sum is accurate to about 50.

- Year-end rebuild: revolver capacity 960 + 5,500 = 6,460; implied drawn revolver = 11,949 principal - (413 + 4,300 + 729 + 2,000 + 2,500 = 9,942 term loans) = 2,007; availability 6,460 - 2,007 - 26 collateralised letters of credit = 4,427, consistent with the printed "approximately $4.4 billion". Using the printed 2,100 outstanding on the Revolving Loan C gives 4,334; the difference arises from rounded inputs.
- Change in credit facility principal March to June 2026: 12,453 - 11,665 = 788; fall in availability 4,600 - 3,700 = 900.
### Maturities and class movements

- 2026 tie-out: 750 + (25 + 227 + 8 + 20 + 25 = 305) = 1,055. 2027: 3,250 + 305 = 3,555 (so the Revolving Loan B was undrawn). 2028 notes 2,500 + 1,000 + 1,250 = 4,750; remainder 642 less 280 of other amortisation = 362 for Term A-6 (413 - 25 - 25 = 363 by schedule). 2029 notes 1,500 + 1,500 + 1,250 + 1,250 + 1,500 = 7,000 plus about 280 amortisation = 7,279.

- Series tie-out: CCO Holdings 27,250; Charter Operating 44,500; TWC, LLC 9,918; TWCE 1,000; subtotal 82,668; plus credit facilities 11,949 = 94,617. Secured notes 44,500 + 9,918 + 1,000 = 55,418, matching the secured notes line.

- Class movement December 31, 2025 to June 30, 2026: unsecured 27,250 - 26,734 = 516 (3,000 issued and 3,000 redeemed net to zero); secured 55,418 - 54,658 = 760, of which the sterling notes were remeasured from 842 + 876 = 1,718 to 829 + 862 = 1,691, a 27 reduction, so repurchases were 733; total repurchases 516 + 733 = 1,249, consistent with the stated 1.2 billion. Total change 93,845 - 94,617 = -772 = -1,249 + 504 (credit facilities) - 27 (sterling remeasurement).
### Tie-outs

- Balance sheet, June 30, 2026: total current liabilities 12,868 + long-term debt 92,960 + equipment installment plan facility 1,596 + deferred income taxes 68 + other long-term liabilities 3,342 + total member's equity 42,605 = 153,439 total assets.
- Cox figure differences: 12.6 - 12.4 = 0.2 billion; 4.2 - 4.0 = 0.2 billion; 3.5 billion + 650 = 4,150 against the stated 4.2 billion (rounded).
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation |

| No filing or release after July 24, 2026: no September 30, 2026 balance sheet, leverage, liquidity or covenant figure, and no Cox closing status | High | CP-1A, CP-2, CP-5 | Supply the Q3 2026 10-Q and any 8-K to November 5, 2026, or confirm none |

| Current series-level debt and maturity ladder not supplied; 1,249 of repurchases are not mapped to series and amortisation paid in 2026 is not itemised | High | CP-2 | Supply a current debt schedule or the next 10-Q debt note |

| Covenant ratios after December 31, 2025 not printed; covenant EBITDA, management fees (rounded to 0.1 billion) and indenture definitions not supplied | High | CP-2, CP-5 | Supply compliance certificates, the Charter Operating credit agreement and the indentures |
| Facility-level availability and letters of credit at June 30, 2026 not printed; December 31, 2024 availability not printed | Medium | CP-2 | Supply the facility schedule at the latest date |

| Whether the 256 mortgage note is in the debt figure and the equipment installment plan facility's revolving-period renewal date are not stated | Medium | CP-2 | Supply the note terms and the facility amendment |

| Issuer share of the 17,122 contractual obligations (the table includes parent companies) and operating leases after December 31, 2025 not supplied | Medium | CP-2 | Supply issuer-level commitments |

| Whether the issuer or the parent funds the approximately 4.2 billion Cox cash price (the 10-Q says "we" but names Charter and Charter Holdings as payers) is ambiguous | Medium | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply the Transaction Agreement financing terms and any commitment papers |

| Cox and Liberty Broadband agreements, the Cox EBITDA and any pro forma leverage not supplied, so no post-closing leverage is computed | Medium | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply the agreements, the proxy statement and Cox financials |
| Adjusted EBITDA is a company non-GAAP measure with other add-backs ("Other, net" of 792 in FY2025); no reconciliation to covenant EBITDA | Medium | CP-2, CP-5 | Treat ratios as indicative |
| No discrete Q3 or Q4 2025 statements and no June 30, 2025 balance sheet; Q4 2025 values are derived by difference | Low | CP-1 | Use 9M and FY differences as labelled |
| Text extraction only; original HTML and XBRL not supplied | Low | CP-5 | Spot-check flagged tables against the filed documents |
## Next module

- CP-1A: take the single reportable segment, product-line revenue, customer trends, ownership chain, guarantor and collateral structure and the Cox and Liberty Broadband transactions from this handoff; show both the 12.6 and 12.4 billion Cox debt figures and the 4.0 and 4.2 billion cash figures with their dates; carry the Cox payer ambiguity and the lack of post-July 24, 2026 evidence.

- CP-2: start from the debt-by-instrument table, the maturity roll-forward, the liquidity table and the covenant table; treat 1,596 of equipment installment plan financing, 1,155 of short-term borrowings and the leases and commitments as claims outside the debt figure; do not compare the computed ratios with covenant levels; carry the missing indentures and credit agreement, the rounded management fees and the unmapped repurchases as limits.

- CP-5: trace every figure to the locators given; flag that LTM, derived-quarter, ratio, roll-forward and proxy rows are calculated, not reported, and that availability figures are rounded to 0.1 billion.

## Request

- Question: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to a creditor of CCO Holdings, LLC, and what do they mean for risk and structure? Reader: the credit committee reading the fact pack first.

- Perimeter: CCO Holdings, LLC and its consolidated subsidiaries as in its own 10-K and 10-Qs. The pending Cox Transactions and the Liberty Broadband Combination are agreements of the parent, Charter Communications, Inc., and its subsidiary Charter Holdings; they are described here because the issuer's own filings describe their effect on the guaranteed and secured debt group. Consistency with CP-0 and CP-1: this answer confirms both and refines two points. First, CP-0 and CP-1 logged the Cox cash figures of 4.0 billion (10-K) and 4.2 billion (10-Qs) without a source for the difference, and CP-0 said the components in the 10-Q do not equal 4.0 billion. The sources do explain it: the cash component payable by Charter Holdings is 500 in the Q3 2025 10-Q and the 10-K and 650 in the Q1 and Q2 2026 10-Qs, so 3,500 + 500 = 4,000 and 3,500 + 650 = 4,150, which the 2026 10-Qs round to 4.2 billion. The filings do not say why it changed. Second, the 12.6 billion assumed Cox net debt in the 10-K is stated "on a pro forma basis contemplating Cox Communications refinancing of debt maturities occurring between signing and closing", while the Q3 2025 and 2026 10-Qs give 12.4 billion without that qualifier; CP-1 reported both without this explanation. The 10-K also states that Charter, not the issuer, "is obligated to fund $4.0 billion of cash consideration" (10-K page:64), which narrows the payer question CP-1 left open (the new indebtedness issuer is still not stated). No figure in CP-0 or CP-1 is changed.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| CCO Holdings is the holding company of Charter's Spectrum cable business, with 77.74% residential revenue and shrinking Internet and video customers offset by mobile growth. The pending Cox Transactions may add guaranteed, secured debt ahead of its unsecured notes. | Medium | Transaction agreements, the post-closing structure and anything after July 24, 2026 are not in the sources; the entity chart is an image and was not extracted. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The issuer is owned entirely by CCH I Holdings, LLC within Charter's chain and has one reportable segment managed centrally. | Control and cash sit with the parent; creditors depend on subsidiary cash flow and parent distribution policy. | High |

| Internet customers fell to 29,388 thousand from 29,908 thousand while mobile lines rose to 12,540 thousand from 10,856 thousand over twelve months. | Mobile growth supports revenue, but Internet and video erosion lowers revenue and EBITDA, so leverage rises mechanically. | High |

| The issuer's subsidiaries are the primary funding source for Charter's share repurchases through distributions to parent companies. | Creditor protection rests on indenture leverage tests and Charter's stated leverage range, not on a hard cap. | High |

| The Cox Transactions are pending; the issuer's filings expect Cox notes to become guaranteed and secured debt, and the Cox cash figure moved from 4.0 billion to 4.2 billion. | More claims would rank ahead of the issuer's unsecured notes; Cox earnings and the post-closing perimeter are not supplied. | Medium |

| In 2026 unsecured notes fell 516 while credit facilities rose 504. | Debt shifted from unsecured to secured, lowering the standing of remaining unsecured notes without any non-pro-rata exchange. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

CCO Holdings is a holding company whose principal assets are the equity of its operating subsidiaries, which deliver Spectrum Internet, Mobile, TV and Voice to residential and business customers in 41 states under a single reportable segment. It is wholly owned by CCH I Holdings, LLC and sits inside Charter's chain; it has no sponsor, no listed equity and no public ownership of its own. Its business is a mature, subscription-based, capital-intensive network operator: about 89% of revenue is monthly subscription fees, residential revenue is 77.74% of FY2025 revenue, and revenue is drifting down slightly (Q2 2026 revenue 13,526 against 13,766) because Internet and video customers are eroding faster than mobile lines and commercial revenue grow. The creditor-relevant structure is the more important feature. Of the issuer's 93,845 of principal debt at June 30, 2026, 67,111 is secured and guaranteed by the issuer and the operating group, while its own 26,734 of unsecured notes are structurally and effectively subordinated, and the issuer's subsidiaries are the primary funding source for Charter's buybacks through distributions. The transaction that matters is the pending Cox acquisition by Charter and Charter Holdings: the issuer's filings say Cox's unsecured notes are expected to become guaranteed and secured debt and Cox entities to become Obligors, which would add claims ahead of the issuer's unsecured notes while the filings do not show where Cox's earnings will sit. The Liberty Broadband Combination is a second pending parent-level transaction. Nothing is supplied after July 24, 2026, so closing status, Cox financing and any new issuance since June are unknown.
### Company and operating model
| Area | Fact | Category | Locator | Credit relevance |

| Core activity | Broadband connectivity company: Spectrum Internet, Mobile, TV and Voice for residential and small to large business customers; "nearly 59 million homes and small to large businesses across 41 states" at June 30, 2026 (58 million at December 31, 2025). | Documentary Fact | 10-Q Jun 2026 page:16; 10-K page:5 | Scale across a wide footprint; revenue is not tied to one region. |

| Revenue model | About 89% of revenue in FY2025 and FY2024 is monthly subscription fees for Internet, mobile, video, voice and commercial services plus regional sports and news channels; subscriptions can generally be discontinued at any time. The other 11% is advertising, franchise and regulatory fees collected for authorities, device sales, processing and installation fees and similar. | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:84 | Recurring revenue is high, but low contractual lock-in means customer losses reduce revenue quickly. |

| Revenue mix FY2025 | Internet 23,765, mobile service 3,762, video 13,703, voice 1,350, commercial 7,315, advertising 1,468, other 3,411 of 54,774; residential revenue 42,580. Internet is 43.39%, video 25.02%, mobile 6.87% (calculated). | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:162 | Video is a quarter of revenue and declining; Internet is the largest line. |

| Q2 2026 trend | Q2 2026 revenue 13,526 against 13,766: Internet 5,776 against 5,969 (down 3.2%), video 3,149 against 3,488 (down 9.7%), mobile service 1,095 against 921 (up 18.9%), commercial 1,865 against 1,836, advertising 416 against 371. | Documentary Fact | 10-Q Jun 2026 page:13, page:21 | Mobile and commercial growth offset only part of Internet and video decline. |

| Customers | June 30, 2026 against June 30, 2025 (thousands): customer relationships 31,499 against 32,060; Internet 29,388 against 29,908; mobile lines 12,540 against 10,856; video 12,524 against 12,631; voice 5,694 against 6,386. In Q2 2026 Internet fell 172,000 and mobile lines rose 406,000. | Documentary Fact | 10-Q Jun 2026 page:18 to page:20 | Penetration is falling in the core product; mobile growth is the offset. |

| Pricing | Standardised Spectrum pricing and bundles with multi-year guaranteed pricing and speed options, moving from "lower promotional and persistent bundled pricing" to drive growth. Monthly residential revenue per residential customer was $117.52 against $119.70 (down 1.8%, calculated). | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:16 to page:17; 10-Q Jun 2026 page:18 to page:19 | Pricing is being used to defend volume, so revenue per customer is not rising. |

| Video economics | Programming costs were 2,035 against 2,253 in Q2 2026, 25% against 27% of operating costs; costs allocated to programmer streaming applications are netted within video revenue (184 in Q2). Media consolidation has given programmers "additional selling power". | Documentary Fact | 10-Q Jun 2026 page:22, page:24; 10-K page:22 | Programming cost falls with customers and the allocation, so video revenue decline is partly cost-neutral. |

| Mobile model | Spectrum Mobile uses customers' WiFi, 49 million out-of-home WiFi access points and the Verizon cellular network; a July 2025 agreement with T-Mobile US, Inc. is set to deliver mobile services to Spectrum Business customers from 2026; customers can pay for devices under interest-free monthly installment plans financed through the equipment installment plan facility. | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:10, page:17; 10-Q Jun 2026 page:11 to page:13 | Mobile depends on a third-party network and device financing, adding working capital and secured borrowing (CP-1). |

| Commercial and other | Spectrum Business (small business, and mid-market and large business including wholesale to carriers), Spectrum Reach advertising, regional sports networks (Los Angeles Lakers rights through 2032; SportsNet LA affiliate and advertising agreements through 2038; a 35.0% interest in Sterling Entertainment Enterprises, LLC), over 35 local news channels and Spectrum Community Solutions. | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:13 to page:16 | Diversifies revenue; sports rights are long fixed commitments. |

| Competition | AT&T and Verizon are the primary fiber-to-the-home competitors with overlap in approximately 27% and 16% of the operating footprint; fixed wireless, satellite, DSL, virtual MVPDs and direct broadcast satellite also compete; national mobile operators are expanding 5G and converged offers. | Management Language | 10-K page:22 to page:24 | Competitive intensity explains the Internet customer losses and caps pricing. |

| Network and capital intensity | Hybrid fiber coaxial network with a network evolution programme (1.2 GHz then 1.8 GHz spectrum, high split, DAA, DOCSIS 4.0) "largely complete by the end of 2027"; capital expenditure was 11,624 in FY2025 and 5,713 in 6M 2026, and about 11.4 billion is expected for 2026 excluding Cox. | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:6 to page:7, page:18; 10-Q Jun 2026 page:37 | A fixed capital programme absorbs cash that would otherwise reduce debt (CP-1). |

| Subsidised rural build | Since 2022 the issuer has spent $7.7 billion and activated about 1.3 million passings; it expects to invest over $8 billion in total, of which over $2 billion of support has been awarded; failure to meet build-out milestones "could subject us to financial penalties". Spend was 391 in Q2 2026 and 818 in 6M 2026. | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:19 to page:20; 10-Q Jun 2026 page:19 | Capital is committed ahead of subsidy receipt and carries milestone penalty risk. |

| Cost structure | Q2 2026 operating costs and expenses 8,236: programming 2,035, other costs of revenue 1,837, field and technology operations 1,313, customer operations 785, marketing and residential sales 927, stock compensation 138, Cox transition expenses 65, other 1,136. Over 80% of customer premise service transactions are handled by the in-house field workforce; about 91,900 full-time equivalent employees at December 31, 2025. | Documentary Fact | 10-Q Jun 2026 page:14; 10-K page:20, page:39 | Costs are largely fixed in the short run; transition costs rise ahead of Cox. |

| Working capital | Accounts receivable, net 3,580 and accrued capital expenditures 3,162 at June 30, 2026; equipment installment plan receivables of about 1.4 billion current and 1.2 billion noncurrent; supply chain finance obligations 725 and deferred payment program 1,155. | Documentary Fact | 10-Q Jun 2026 page:5, page:9 to page:10, page:13 | Vendor and device financing extend payables and receivables; both are claims outside the debt figure (CP-1). |

| Regulation and franchises | Cable franchises are non-exclusive and not guaranteed to renew; retransmission consent and pole attachment rules affect video costs and rural construction; federal pole rules apply in twenty-six states. | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:29 to page:30, page:60 | Franchise loss or higher regulated costs hit local revenue and costs. |

The fourth quarter 2025 impairment analysis found franchise fair value above carrying value "by more than 10%" in each unit; management is monitoring the decline in Charter's stock price. | Documentary Fact | 10-Q Jun 2026 page:5, page:21 | Equity cushion is intangible-heavy; an impairment would not change cash flow but could affect covenants defined on book values (not supplied). |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The principal transaction is the pending Cox acquisition by Charter and Charter Holdings, not by the issuer. On May 16, 2025, Charter, Charter Holdings and Cox Enterprises, Inc. entered into a Transaction Agreement under which Charter buys 100% of certain Cox Communications subsidiaries that conduct its commercial fiber and managed IT and cloud services businesses, and Cox Enterprises contributes Cox Communications' residential cable business to Charter Holdings, with Cox Enterprises paying $1.00 for a new class of Charter Class C common stock (10-Q Jun 2026 page:8). Consideration is 3.5 billion in cash from Charter for the equity sale and, for the contribution, cash from Charter Holdings plus convertible preferred units of Charter Holdings with a 6.0 billion liquidation preference paying 6.875% and about 33.6 million Charter Holdings common units; the cash from Charter Holdings is 650 million in the 2026 10-Qs and 500 million in the 10-K and the Q3 2025 10-Q (10-Q Jun 2026 page:9; 10-K page:28; 10-Q Sep 2025 page:9). The combined entity will assume Cox Communications' approximately 12.4 billion of net debt and finance leases (10-Q Jun 2026 page:9), a figure the 10-K gave as approximately 12.6 billion on a pro forma basis for Cox refinancings between signing and closing (10-K page:28). The status is pending: the June 2026 10-Q uses the future tense throughout, lists the ability to satisfy closing conditions among its risks and gives no closing date; the 10-K lists conditions including Charter stockholder approvals, expiry of the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period and approvals of the Federal Communications Commission and certain local franchise, state franchising and state public utility commission authorities (10-K page:61). Which approvals have been received, the end date and the termination fee amounts are not in the pack (the 10-K says only that Charter "could owe a substantial termination fee" (10-K page:62)).

For creditors the key text is the issuer's own: the 10-Q says the company is "also required to fund approximately $4.2 billion of cash purchase price at the closing of the Cox Transactions" (10-Q Jun 2026 page:27), while the 10-K says "Charter is obligated to fund $4.0 billion of cash consideration under the Transaction Agreement which we expect to fund by incurring indebtedness" (10-K page:64). After closing the issuer "presently expect[s]" that Cox's unsecured notes assumed at closing "will constitute Guaranteed and Secured Debt", that Cox Communications and substantially all of its subsidiaries "will become Obligors", and that all or part of the approximately 4.2 billion of indebtedness issued to finance the cash payment "may constitute Guaranteed and Secured Debt when issued" (10-Q Jun 2026 page:34). Charter and its subsidiaries, including CCO Holdings, are also subject to restrictions on the conduct of their business before closing, including in certain cases the ability to incur certain indebtedness (10-K page:65). The contribution is to Charter Holdings (10-Q Jun 2026 page:8), and the filings do not say whether Cox's operating results will be consolidated in CCO Holdings' statements after closing or sit elsewhere in Charter's structure. That is Insufficient Information, not an adverse conclusion; it matters because Cox debt could be guaranteed inside the Obligor Group, which the issuer guarantees, while Cox earnings might not be in the issuer's own statements. The cash-purchase financing is described only as debt to be incurred; no sources and uses, commitment papers, rating agency actions or liquidity effect are given. Cox transition costs are already in operating results (65 in Q2 2026 and 89 in 6M 2026) with 34 and 37 of transition capital expenditure (10-Q Jun 2026 page:14 to page:15, page:37).

The second pending transaction is the Liberty Broadband Combination, a merger agreement dated November 12, 2024 under which Charter acquires Liberty Broadband Corporation through a merger and upstream merger, with Liberty Broadband becoming a wholly owned subsidiary of Charter (10-Q Jun 2026 page:28). Pending its closing, Charter buys Charter Class A shares from Liberty Broadband monthly, and in May 2026 Charter advanced a term loan of approximately 359 million to Liberty Broadband (10-Q Jun 2026 page:29 to page:30). The 10-K expects additional debt "in connection with the Cox Transactions and Liberty Broadband Combination" and the assumption of indebtedness of Liberty Broadband and its subsidiaries (10-K page:52). The amount and ranking of any Liberty Broadband debt are not stated.

New debt issues in the periods covered: in September 2025 Charter Operating and Charter Communications Operating Capital Corp. jointly issued 1.25 billion of 5.850% senior secured notes due December 2035 at 99.932% and 750 million of 6.700% senior secured notes due December 2055 at 99.832%, with proceeds used for general corporate purposes including repayment of the 6.150% senior secured notes due 2026 and potential buybacks, and a loss on extinguishment of about 28 million (10-K page:155). In January 2026 CCO Holdings and CCO Holdings Capital Corp. jointly issued 1.75 billion of 7.000% senior notes due February 2033 and 1.25 billion of 7.375% senior notes due February 2036, both at par, with proceeds for general corporate purposes including the call of 750 million of the 5.500% notes due 2026 and part (2.25 billion) of the 5.125% notes due 2027 (10-K page:155; 10-Q Mar 2026 page:11). In November 2025 the equipment installment plan facility was amended to extend maturity to November 3, 2029 and raise capacity to 2.0 billion (10-K page:161). In the second quarter of 2026 the company repurchased 1.2 billion of principal of various series on the open market at a gain of about 243 million (10-Q Jun 2026 page:11). No new notes are reported for the first half of 2026 other than the January issuance, and no source reports issuance after June 30, 2026.
### Ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour
| Behaviour or fact | Evidence | Category | Legal capacity, willingness and feasibility | Dimension and locator |

| Control | All membership interests are held by CCH I Holdings, LLC; the issuer is a holding company whose principal assets are equity in operating subsidiaries; Charter, Charter Holdings and Spectrum Management perform financing, cash management, treasury and other services on a centralised basis, and changes in member's equity are treated as contributions and distributions | Documentary Fact | Capacity: the parent controls cash by contributions and distributions. Willingness: set by Charter's capital allocation. | Control and cash management; 10-Q Jun 2026 page:7 |

| Distributions to parent | Distributions to parent were 3,051 in FY2024, 6,794 in FY2025 and 2,460 in 6M 2026 (3,356 in 6M 2025), above free cash flow of 5,827 in FY2025 and 5,070 over the last twelve months (CP-1) | Documentary Fact | Capacity: indentures restrict distributions that fund parent note principal unless no default exists and the leverage ratio test is met; June 30, 2026 test "met". Willingness: distributions exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 and the LTM. Feasibility: leverage 4.22x on CP-1 metrics against a 6.0 indenture maximum. | Distribution policy; 10-K page:159; 10-Q Jun 2026 page:36; CP-1 |

| Funding of parent buybacks | "To the extent such purchases occur, CCO Holdings and its subsidiaries are the primary source for funding such purchases through distributions to their parent companies." Charter bought about 5.5 million Class A shares for about 1.2 billion in 6M 2026 and 2.8 million from Liberty Broadband for about 595 million; remaining board authority 365 million | Documentary Fact | Capacity: not capped by the sources.
